Subject: NimblePay SAR deletion vs. audit log retention — SIG evidence request

Hi Vanessa,

We’re preparing a SIG questionnaire response and ran into a scenario where our regulators require us to honor Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs) to delete user-identifying records, while our payments audit team requires a preserved audit trail for transaction investigations for up to 180 days.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood redact or delete PII from application logs while preserving a separate, non-identifying audit trail for payments?
- What controls do you have to put a "customer hold" on deletion (legal/forensics) so we can freeze retention for a particular tenant?
- Can you provide SIG/CAIQ references or artifacts showing where these controls are documented (or a SOC 2 mapping if available)?

I’ve attached a short spreadsheet with a few SAR scenarios we’re concerned about (Nimble_SAR_Scenarios.xlsx).

Goal: quick confirmation of feasibility and an estimate for how long it would take to produce an evidence bundle (sample export + policy excerpt). Our compliance team would like to give the SIG owner a 2-week turnaround expectation.

Thanks,
Grace Turner

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear examples. Looping in Rishi and Neha for technical and controls evidence. High level reply below; we can follow up with an evidence bundle and a short call if helpful.

Short answer: yes — we support a separation between application-level telemetry that may contain PII and an immutable payments audit trail. Typical approach we recommend:

- Segmented storage: application logs (request traces, user identifiers) are stored in a customer-scoped bucket with a default 30-day TTL. Payments audit logs (transaction events, settlement traces) are written to a separate, append-only ledger with a default 180-day retention.
- Redaction on delete: when a DSAR deletion is requested, we run a targeted redaction workflow that removes user-identifying fields from application logs but leaves transaction audit entries intact (we replace PII with a consistent, irreversible hash/ID placeholder).
- Customer hold/forensics: we have a legal-hold flag you can set at tenant scope that pauses deletion workflows (both scheduled TTL and manual redaction) and flags data for export. Holds are reversible only via authorized change control (RBAC + audit trail).

What we can provide within ~10 business days:
1) SIG/CAIQ pointers and an excerpt from our retention policy (PDF).
2) A sample export (redacted) showing how we separate audit payloads from PII-containing traces.
3) A technical mapping of where rules are enforced (service, queue, policy).

I’ve attached a short overview and will ask Rishi to describe the enforcement points and export mechanics. Can you confirm whether NimblePay will need a temporary extended hold (e.g., 90 days) for the current investigation? If so, include the ticket/PO number and we’ll surface an attestation template.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NimblePay SAR deletion vs. audit log retention — SIG evidence request

Grace — brief technical breakdown so you have concrete language for the SIG:

1) Architecture & separation
- Ingest pipeline tags events as "app_trace" vs "payment_audit" at the API gateway layer. The tag determines downstream routing.
- "app_trace" flows into the customer-scoped encrypted bucket (S3) with lifecycle rules (default 30d) and is subject to PII redaction.
- "payment_audit" events are routed to a write-once ledger service (append-only) and replicated across regions per your tenancy configuration; retention there is 180d by default.

2) Deletion/redaction workflow
- DSAR triggers an idempotent job. For app_trace records we run a deterministic hashing+salt of any PII fields and then remove raw PII from the object body (we retain a hash reference for correlation if needed by legal).
- For payment_audit, we do not remove transaction integrity fields; we can redact customer identifiers to a hashed token but preserve event order and timestamps required for audits.

3) Legal hold / forensic hold
- A tenant-level legal_hold boolean is stored in our control-plane DB. While true, retention controllers will skip deletion jobs and mark objects as "on_hold". Only agents with the "legal:hold:approve" role can clear it; all role changes and hold actions are captured in the audit log.

4) Export mechanics
- Exports are produced via presigned, time-limited S3 URLs to your configured destination. We can provide both redacted and non-identifying audit bundles. Exports include a manifest, sample objects, and a retention attestation PDF.

5) Evidence & docs (what we can attach)
- Retention mapping CSV showing buckets, lifecycle rules, and applicable policies.
- Sample redaction run log (sanitized).
- SOC 2 control IDs mapping to retention and change control processes.

I’ve attached the retention mapping CSV for your reference. Happy to join a call to walk through an evidence bundle if that helps accelerate the SIG review.

—Rishi
